sections.h2: When refinishing makes more sense than replacing
body: Across Lake City, from 1990s subdivisions off the highway to the older streets close to the courthouse, many kitchens have sturdy boxes wearing a tired, yellowed finish. When the doors are solid and the layout still suits you, cabinet refinishing in Lake City, FL delivers a new look with no tear-out and no dumpster. Torn between the two? Our write-up on whether to refinish or replace walks through the good-candidate signs and the deal-breakers.

A cabinet door gets grabbed, splashed, and bumped dozens of times a day, so it earns far more prep than a bedroom wall. We pull every door and drawer face, number each one, and bag the pulls and hinges. Kitchen grease comes off with a degreaser, then every face is scuffed so the next coat has tooth. A bonding primer locks onto the slick factory lacquer, and the finish coat is a waterborne urethane enamel that cures far tougher than wall paint and wipes clean of steam and sticky handprints.

sections.h2: Oak grain, color choice, and matching the room
body: Golden oak turns up in a lot of Columbia County kitchens, and those deep pores telegraph through any paint left unfilled. Some owners like a hint of that texture; others want it gone for a sleek, modern face. The pros and cons of each are in our oak cabinet painting guide. To land on a shade, hand us a drawer front or a store chip and we mix to it, then brush out large drawdown cards for you to hold against the countertop before the sprayer comes out. If the walls need a refresh too, our Lake City interior painting crew can finish the room in the same visit.

sections.h2: Timing and keeping the kitchen usable
body: Since nothing here depends on the weather, cabinet jobs fit any month, and plenty of Lake City households slot them into the hot stretch of summer. Plan on a few days of open shelving and curing enamel. Ahead of day one, your crew lead flags which days cooking will be awkward so you can stock up on takeout or grill outside. Once you sign, the start date typically falls one to three weeks out, and the written quote states how many days the kitchen is out of commission. Ask about low-VOC options if odor is a concern. On the last day we walk the kitchen with you, fix anything you flag, and leave a labelled can for future touch-ups. Our full method is outlined on the main cabinet painting and refinishing service overview or the Lake City contractor page.

faqs.q: Does a painted cabinet finish survive North Florida humidity?
faqs.a: It does when the layers are right. A thorough grease strip, a primer built to bond to factory coatings, and a urethane-modified waterborne enamel together create a shell that shrugs off steam and damp air.

faqs.q: What about the vanity in our bathroom?
faqs.a: Bring it into the scope. A bath vanity is cleaned, primed, and enameled exactly like the kitchen run, and doing both at once keeps the colors consistent.

faqs.q: Can I keep the oak grain from showing?
faqs.a: Yes. Filling the pores ahead of primer gives a flat, furniture-like face; skip that step and a faint grain pattern stays visible under the color.

faqs.q: Can you copy a color from an existing door or swatch?
faqs.a: Sure. A painted door, a paint store chip, or the dregs of an old can all work as a source, and nothing gets sprayed until you sign off on a large sample card.
